answers_to_the_four_questions.bc_ceiling_or_generative_dynamic_range: BC CEILING, now demonstrated on a LEARNABLE task. cube-double has a documented 40-point gap between value-based methods (GCIQL 40 +/- 5) and behavior cloning (GCBC 1 +/- 1). Our arms land on the behavior-cloning side of that gap, matching GCBC. Two tasks, two object counts, 1-100 NFE, generative and non-generative alike: all at the behavior-cloning floor.
answers_to_the_four_questions.does_diffusion_outperform_low_nfe_flow: Not measured on cube-double: the predeclared gate requires stage 1 to show non-trivial performance first, and it did not. On cube-triple diffusion at 100 NFE also scored zero.
answers_to_the_four_questions.does_flow_materially_exceed_the_bc_floor: No. Every arm scores 0/60. On the secondary cube-distance metric the non-generative BC floor is the BEST arm (+0.00355 m versus -0.00133 to +0.00090 m for the generative arms), so generative modeling is not earning its cost here.
answers_to_the_four_questions.does_performance_change_meaningfully_wit: No. Flow at 1, 2, 4 and 8 NFE and Shortcut at 1 and 4 NFE are all 0/60. Verified model calls scale exactly and latency scales 2.84 -> 22.76 ms, so the compute was genuinely spent; the flatness is not an instrumentation artifact.

consequence: Per the predeclared decision rule: stop treating pure-BC OGBench cube manipulation as the main benchmark. The next research question is whether value guidance is fundamentally required, or whether entity-structured generative policies can improve matters without a critic.
interpretation: This is the decisive result the cube-triple experiment could not provide. On cube-triple nothing works for anyone, so zero was uninformative. On cube-double a 40-point gap exists between value-based methods (GCIQL 40%) and behavior cloning (GCBC 1%), and our arms land on the BC side of that gap. The limitation is therefore the POLICY-LEARNING PARADIGM (behavior cloning without a critic), not the generative objective and not the inference budget.
key_finding: On cube-double -- a task where published value-based methods reach 40% -- both the non-generative BC floor and flow matching score 0/60. Published GCBC also scores 1 +/- 1 here. So our arms again reproduce the published behavior-cloning baseline, on a task that is demonstrably learnable by other means.
secondary_observation: Shortcut clips 11.8-13.2% of steps versus 3.1-8.8% for BC and Flow, i.e. it emits substantially more extreme actions, and still places no cube. This mirrors the cube-triple diffusion arm (20.1% clipping, zero cubes) and further weakens the action-saturation lead as a sufficient explanation.
why_this_is_decisive: cube-triple could not discriminate because no published method exceeds 4% there, so zero was uninformative. cube-double is solvable -- value-based methods reach 40% -- so a zero here is informative rather than vacuous. What is established: within this pure-imitation setup, changing the generative objective (BC / Flow / Shortcut) and spending 1->8 inference calls produces no measurable task-performance gain, because every arm sits at the BC floor. What is NOT established: that behavior cloning without a critic is the causal binding constraint. Published value-based results (GCIQL 40 vs GCBC 1) strongly suggest the learning objective matters, but we did not run a critic here, so that causal claim is not isolated by our own measurements.
